gaps.sentence: My grandfather was ___ engineer during the war.
gaps.explanation: 'An engineer' — 'engineer' begins with a vowel sound.

gaps.sentence: ___ noise woke me up in the middle of the night.
gaps.explanation: 'The noise' — the one that woke me; 'in the night' is a fixed phrase.

gaps.sentence: ___ sales figures for October look promising.
gaps.explanation: 'The sales figures for October' — defined by the for-phrase.

gaps.sentence: ___ rich often object to paying inheritance tax.
gaps.explanation: 'The rich' = rich people as a group.

gaps.sentence: I saw ___ film last night, and the film was about mountain climbers.
gaps.hint: first mention of one of many
gaps.explanation: First mention of a countable noun takes 'a'; the second mention becomes 'the' (already written out here).

gaps.sentence: He was ___ last person to leave the building.
gaps.explanation: Ordinals take 'the': the last person, the first time.

gaps.sentence: He plays ___ violin in the youth orchestra.
___ unemployment has fallen sharply this year.
gaps.explanation: Unemployment as a general concept takes no article.
